ledger.note: 1540: Mạc Đăng Dung submits to the Ming and cedes land. 'Under Ming pressure, Mạc Đăng Dung submitted' in 1540 (Mạc dynasty and Mạc Đăng Dung pages: 'The Ming Chinese threatened Mạc Đăng Dung with an invasion of 110,000 men'); the Lê-Mạc War page dates it 'at Nam Quan Pass in 1541' and says 'He ceded half of Quảng Ninh province to China'. The north-east around Móng Cái is the reading of 'half'; the other pages say only 'ceding land'. The Ming downgraded his polity to a chieftaincy and accepted him 'as ruler of part of Vietnam'.

1573: the Mạc retake Thăng Long, 'a year later'.

ledger.note: February 1592: the Southern court launches its last offensive. 'In February 1592, the Southern dynasty launched a large northward offensive against the Northern Mạc.'

region.text: Đông Kinh and the Mạc north outside Cao Bằng

ledger.note: 1592: the Mạc lose Đông Kinh and the north. 'In 1592, Đông Kinh, the capital of the Mạc dynasty, was reconquered by the Later Lê forces'; the Lê-Trịnh army captured Lào Cai, Yên Bái and Phú Thọ on 14 November and arrested and executed Mạc Mậu Hợp at Hải Dương on 25 November 1592; the remnants fled to Bắc Cạn and Cao Bằng.

region.text: the Mạc north outside Cao Bằng

ledger.note: April 1593: the Lê emperor returns to Đông Kinh. 'In April 1593, the southern emperor Lê Thế Tông was welcomed back to Đông Kinh (Hanoi)'; Mạc Kính Chỉ's army was destroyed 'a year later'.

1677: the Trịnh take Cao Bằng. 'The Mạc in Cao Bằng were completely defeated by the Trịnh clan in 1677'; Mạc Kính Vũ fled into Guangxi after the Battle of Cao Bình 'and the Qing agreed to arrest him'. The Kangxi Emperor had 'demanded in 1667 that Trịnh Tạc return Cao Bằng Province to the Mạc' and 'In 1673, the Qing had lost interest in mediating'.
1677: the Mạc dynasty ends. 'the demise of the Mạc dynasty' followed the defeat at Cao Bình; Cliopatria's Đại Việt row goes on to 1833 with the Cham remnant at Phan Rang, which is not Mạc land.

wars.outcome: The Revival Lê dynasty wins: it recovers the south by 1533-1554, Đông Kinh in 1592 and, through the Trịnh, Cao Bằng in 1677; the Mạc rump survives in Cao Bằng under Ming and Qing support.
wars.note: The page dates the two phases 1533-1593 and 1593-1677. Fronts: Lê-Trịnh south of the Red River by January 1560; the Mạc back to the Cả River in 1571; Thăng Long taken in 1572 and retaken in 1573; the Mã River clashes to 1583; Đông Kinh lost in 1592.

wars.name: Ming intervention against the Mạc

zones.text: the north-east of Quảng Ninh around Móng Cái, 'half of Quảng Ninh province'

wars.outcome: The Jiajing Emperor sends 125,000 soldiers to the border in 1537 at the Lê request (Lê-Mạc War page) and threatens 110,000 men from Guangxi; Mạc Đăng Dung submits in 1540, cedes land and is downgraded to a governor, and the Ming accept him as ruler of part of Vietnam.
wars.note: The Lê-Mạc War page dates the submission 1541.

wars.name: Lê attack on Cao Bằng (1627)
wars.outcome: Mạc Kính Khoan surrenders and accepts the Lê title Thông quốc công; the Mạc nevertheless hold Cao Bằng to 1677 (the page is silent on 1627-1638).

wars.name: Qing mediation over Cao Bằng and the Trịnh conquest
wars.outcome: The Kangxi Emperor demands in 1667 that Trịnh Tạc return Cao Bằng to the Mạc, loses interest by 1673; the Trịnh defeat the Mạc in 1677 and Mạc Kính Vũ flees to Guangxi.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages: the Ming-Mạc frontier of 1540 is a cession of 'land' without a boundary, the Lê-Mạc front moved by campaign, and Cliopatria's outlines are 16-km cells. The Red River is the dividing line most often named.

Page budget 5 for 12 shapes: Mạc dynasty, Lê-Mạc War, Mạc Đăng Dung, Champa, Đại Việt. WebFetch summaries were used, so the quotes are the summariser's quotations of each page. None of the five pages gives an area; the infobox comparison could not be made.

What the Cliopatria row is. Its Name 'Đại Việt' (Wikipedia 'Mạc dynasty;Đại Việt', Q1317991) covers three different things: (1) the Mạc dynasty's realm 1527-1677, whole until the Lê restoration of 1533, then the north, then the Cao Bằng rump from 1592; (2) nothing at all for 1678-1682 once the Mạc were gone; (3) from 1653 to 1833 a 12-13 cell strip around Phan Rang (Ninh Thuận) that is Panduranga, the last Cham principality, which Cliopatria hands to this row when its Chámpa row ends in 1652. I wrote the dossier for (1): the Mạc dynasty, state 1527-1677, slug ai-viet kept because the validator and the seed key on it; shapes 1683-1830 are verdict wrong with Panduranga as the correction. The slug and name could be changed by the orchestrator to mac-dynasty, but the Cliopatria name Đại Việt belongs to the whole Vietnamese state of 1054-1804 (Lý, Trần, Hồ, Lê), which Cliopatria spreads over ngo-dynasty, le-dynasty, trinh-lords and nguyen-lords.

Disagreements. (a) Far south: the le-dynasty dossier and Cliopatria give the Lê the whole south from 1533-1534, but the Lê-Mạc War page has the Lê regain Thuận Hóa and Quảng Nam only in 1554; this dossier holds Quảng Bình to Bình Định and the highlands for the Mạc to 1553 (keyframes _1533 and _1540b, loss of 1554). If the gap-filler prefers the le-dynasty reading, delete the 1554 loss and extend _1533. (b) The Nam Quan submission 1540 (Mạc dynasty, Mạc Đăng Dung pages) against 1541 (Lê-Mạc War); the cession 'half of Quảng Ninh province' (Lê-Mạc War page only) is placed around Móng Cái with a 45 km radius, confidence 2; the other pages say only 'ceding land'. (c) The usurpation 15 June (infobox) or 18 June 1527 (Lê-Mạc War). (d) Ming recognition of Cao Bằng 1598 (Mạc page) or the embassy of 1597 (Lê-Mạc War). (e) Mạc dynasty 1527-1592 in some sources, 1527-1677 on the Mạc and Đại Việt pages.

Ming relationship: the Mạc page's status is 'Tributary state of China Ming (1527-1644)'; after 1540 the Ming downgraded Annam to a pacification commission and the Mạc to a governor, which the ming-dynasty dossier should carry as a vassal_start/vassal_end 1540-1598 (counterpart ai-viet) and the Qing from 1662 as a protector of the Cao Bằng rump.

Not drawn: the Mạc governors of the far south; the highland vassals; the Lan Xang and Laos frontier (Lê loyalists lived in Lan Xang 1527-1533); Mạc Kính Điển's naval raids of 1555 and 1557 (no ground); Trần Cảo's rebellion (before 1527). Rulers: gap 1625-1638 at Cao Bằng; Mạc Kính Khoan (surrendered 1627) is not listed with years.

Counterparts: trinh-lords is Cliopatria's Trịnh row (1572-1787) used for events from 1559, when the Trịnh already led the Lê court (Đại Việt page: Trịnh lords 1545-1786); le-dynasty for 1527-1554 events. The Cham strip: champa dossier (champa_1653, champa_1695). Gazetteer: Quàng Nam, Thừa Thiên - Huế and Ha Tinh are the Natural Earth spellings; Móng Cái is not a gazetteer place and is used by coordinates.
